question.text: Will SRS or DOE have publicly stated a cause for the October 28, 2026 Savannah River National Laboratory fire by November 13, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, at any time from October 28, 2026 through November 13, 2026, Savannah River Site (SRS), the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), Savannah River National Laboratory (SRNL), or an on-the-record representative of any of them publicly identified a cause of the October 28, 2026 fire at SRNL — that is, named the mechanism or condition that started the fire (for example an electrical fault, battery failure, equipment malfunction, chemical reaction, hot work, or arson) as its cause, probable cause, suspected cause, or preliminary finding. The statement may appear in an SRS news release listed at https://public.srs.gov/category/news-releases/ (or in the SRS notification banner at https://public.srs.gov/), on a DOE or SRNL website, or be attributed to one of those entities in reporting by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). Statements that the cause is still under investigation, unknown, or undetermined — and statements that only describe when, or in which room of the laboratory, the fire began — do not resolve Yes. If no qualifying statement has appeared by 11:59 p.m. US Eastern Time on November 13, 2026, the question resolves No.
question.fine_print: Statements by Savannah River Nuclear Solutions (SRNS, the SRS management contractor) or by SRNL's operating contractor count as statements by SRS. Unattributed leaks, reporting based solely on unnamed sources, and statements by advocacy groups (such as SRS Watch) or by individual SRS/DOE employees speaking in a personal capacity do not count.

research:
As of November 3-4, 2026, I found no statement from SRS, DOE, SRNL or SRNS naming a cause for the October 28 fire. The only official word on cause is that an investigation is underway.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-03/04: The SRS news-release page lists three releases about the event, all dated 2026-10-28 (#1 at 6:21 PM, #2 at 7:30 PM, #3 at 9:45 PM). The only releases after that are both dated 2026-11-02 and are unrelated: a new NNSA Field Office Manager (Betty L. Huck) and 2027 public tours. None mentions a cause. [SRS news releases](https://public.srs.gov/category/news-releases/)
- 2026-11-03/04: The SRS homepage still features News Release #3. I saw no notification-banner text about a cause. [SRS homepage](https://public.srs.gov/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. Every source I found, dated October 29 to 31, says the cause has not been announced.
- 2026-10-29: Monte Volk, a public affairs officer for DOE's Office of Environmental Management, said: "An investigation into the cause of the fire is underway." He also said the fire was contained, "with no radiological release or employee exposure to radiological contamination." [Post and Courier/Aiken Standard](https://www.postandcourier.com/aikenstandard/aikenstandard/news/local/srnl-fire-srs-emergency-response/article_35bcf1f0-7957-470b-8d5c-5c89a441419c.html)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-31: The Current (also carried by GPB) reported that SRNL and DOE had not responded to requests for comment "other than the fact that an investigation of the fire is underway." The size, cause and materials involved are unconfirmed. [The Current](https://thecurrentga.org/2026/10/31/as-safety-oversight-wanes-and-nuclear-missions-accelerate-a-fire-erupts-at-savannah-river-site/), [GPB](https://www.gpb.org/news/2026/10/29/safety-oversight-wanes-and-nuclear-missions-accelerate-fire-erupts-at-savannah)
- 2026-10-30: A summary piece said officials had not identified the room, whether Building 773-A was involved, or what burned. [Autonocion](https://www.autonocion.com/us/75-year-old-nuclear-lab-fire-one-room-310-square-mile-site-emergency-four-hours-fire-water-pipes/)
- 2026-10-29/30: The AP story (updated October 30) gives no cause. Outside expert Dave Lochbaum said finding the cause could take time. [AP via Local3News](https://www.local3news.com/local-news/georgia/watchdogs-raise-alarms-about-fire-at-south-carolina-site-where-us-plans-to-build-nuclear/article_79ca1bd3-ff73-56a4-8fd6-93428951c663.html)
- 2026-10-29: WRDW pointed to earlier DNFSB findings on SRNL fire suppression, but says nothing public links them to this fire. The reversal on the "radiological release" is still unexplained. [WRDW](https://www.wrdw.com/2026/10/29/what-we-know-about-emergency-savannah-river-site/)
- Other reports on the watchdog angle and the injury also give no cause: [Yahoo](https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/watchdog-cites-earlier-fire-safety-001554587.html), [SC Public Radio](https://www.southcarolinapublicradio.org/sc-news/2026-10-28/savannah-river-site-reopens-to-incoming-traffic-after-fire-sparks-emergency-response), [Augusta Press](https://theaugustapress.com/fire-at-savannah-river-site-injures-employee-prompts-emergency/)
- I found no articles from November 1-3 with new official statements.

## 4. Base rates
- The closest past case is the January 10, 2006 flash fire with an injury at SRNL. DOE handled it as a formal Type B Accident Investigation, and the cause was laid out in the investigation report, not in early press statements. I did not check exactly when that report came out or whether an earlier preliminary cause was given. [DOE Type B report](https://www.energy.gov/node/902681)
- Local reporting says DOE investigations into cause, equipment performance and procedural compliance usually take weeks to months. [WRDW](https://www.wrdw.com/2026/10/29/what-we-know-about-emergency-savannah-river-site/)
- A preliminary cause could surface earlier in a DNFSB weekly site report, but that would come from DNFSB, not from SRS or DOE. It would only count if the report attributes the cause to SRS or DOE.
- So far SRS and DOE have said very little: no room, no building, no materials. I could not find a systematic base rate for how often DOE sites name a preliminary cause within 16 days.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the market prices collected for this brief cover this event. They are Rocket Lab, Port of Savannah and similar markets, and none apply.
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on the cause of the SRNL fire.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution (November 13)
- DNFSB Savannah River weekly site representative reports: the reports covering the weeks ending October 30 and November 6 could describe the event, which might lead to on-the-record follow-up from SRS. I could not find them yet.
- WRDW is still pressing SRS on why it reversed the release account. Follow-up stories could bring out on-the-record comments.
- Congressional or state (SC Emergency Management Division) questions about the release reversal could add pressure for more disclosure.
- The SRS Citizens Advisory Board meets on November 17, which is after the deadline.

DNFSB weekly reports often describe causes within about 1-3 weeks, but DNFSB statements do not count here unless the cause is attributed to SRS, DOE or a contractor. [Santa Fe New Mexican](https://www.santafenewmexican.com/news/local_news/small-overnight-fire-in-lanl-plutonium-facility-burned-itself-out/article_7bb1bd5c-c147-11ef-90a0-abb2d5070522.html)
- So far the public messaging from SRS and DOE on this event has been minimal: three releases, no details on room or material, and a "no comment beyond an investigation" stance six days after the fire.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the markets supplied (Kalshi Rocket Lab, Powell, Port of Savannah and others; Polymarket Savannah State basketball) is related to this question.
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on the cause of the SRNL fire.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution (by 2026-11-13)
- DNFSB Savannah River weekly reports for the weeks ending about Oct 30 and Nov 6 are usually posted 1-2 weeks later on dnfsb.gov. They may describe a cause and attribute it to SRNS, which local outlets could then pick up. Whether that counts depends on how it is attributed.

- Possible congressional or state inquiries, given the controversy over the radiological release report and the South Carolina Emergency Management Division's account.
- The SRS Citizens Advisory Board meeting on 2026-11-17 is after the deadline.
- A DOE accident investigation (Type A or B) report would almost certainly come after November 13.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 10 days remain, until 11:59 p.m. ET on November 13, 2026. For Yes, SRS, DOE, SRNL or SRNS, or an on-the-record spokesperson for one of them, must publicly name a mechanism or condition as the cause, probable cause or preliminary cause of the fire. Examples would be an electrical fault, a chemical reaction or an equipment malfunction. The statement can come in a news release, the site banner, or on-the-record comments reported by credible outlets. Saying the cause is "under investigation" does not count.

(b) The status quo is No. Six days after the fire, the only official word is that "an investigation into the cause of the fire is underway." Officials have not even named the room, the building or the materials involved.

(c) Base rate: when a DOE site fire leads to a formal emergency declaration and an injury, the cause is usually set out in a Type B or similar accident investigation report weeks to months later. In some cases sites do give a preliminary cause within days in reply to press questions, such as "a fume hood fire involving a heating element." That is less common when the site is being guarded and a formal investigation is open. I estimate roughly 15-20% of such events get a publicly named preliminary cause within about 2.5 weeks.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - The press is pressing hard. WRDW keeps asking about the reversal on the radiological release, and the AP, The Current and GPB are following the story.
  - The SC Emergency Management Division and members of Congress may push for answers.
  - DNFSB weekly reports could prompt SRS to confirm a cause on the record.
- For No:
  - DOE's only comment on cause, on October 29, was that it is under investigation.
  - On October 31, SRNL and DOE had not answered requests for comment beyond that.
  - No cause-related release appeared from November 1 to 3. The only new releases, on November 2, were unrelated.
  - The site is visibly limiting disclosure, which fits with the controversy over the reversed release account.
  - The first public forum, the Citizens Advisory Board meeting on November 17, falls after the deadline.

(e) Scenarios:
- No: The investigation continues quietly and SRS issues no further releases. Reporters get "under investigation" answers, and any DNFSB report describing the event is either not attributed to SRS or comes out after November 13.
- Yes: A DNFSB weekly report notes that SRNS attributed the fire to a failed piece of lab equipment. WRDW or the Aiken Standard then gets an SRNS spokesperson to confirm "a preliminary finding of an electrical malfunction in laboratory equipment."

(f) I start from about 15-18%. I adjust down because six days have already passed with complete silence, the site seems defensive amid the release-reversal controversy, and less than half the window remains. I leave a small allowance for press pressure and DNFSB-prompted confirmation, and that brings me to about 10%.

Probability: 10%

Saying "under investigation" does not count.

(b) If nothing changes, the question resolves No. As of November 3-4, the only official word on cause is that "an investigation into the cause of the fire is underway" (DOE EM spokesperson Monte Volk, October 29). No release since October 28 has added anything.

(c) Base rate: I looked at DOE site fires and incidents with injuries or emergency declarations where the agency disclosed little at first. A cause is rarely named publicly within about two weeks. Causes usually come out through formal investigation reports weeks or months later, as with the 2006 SRNL flash fire Type B investigation. Sometimes a spokesperson gives a quick preliminary description such as "an electrical component." My rough estimate is 10-20% for a qualifying statement within 16 days.

  - DNFSB weekly reports could prompt SRS to comment on the record.
- For No:

(e) Scenarios:
- No: SRS stays with "under investigation." The DNFSB weekly report describes the event, but SRS does not confirm the cause on the record, and details come out at the November 17 Citizens Advisory Board meeting or later.
- Yes: Under pressure over the release reversal, an SRNS spokesperson tells WRDW or the Aiken Standard that the fire appears to have started from an electrical fault in lab equipment, with the investigation continuing.

(f) I start from a base rate of about 15%. I adjust down slightly because the site has been unusually secretive and a week has already passed with no new details. I adjust up slightly because the criteria are lenient (any "suspected cause" counts) and media scrutiny is high. Net, I end up around 12%.
